bio_text: Lewis Hamilton is a British driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 2007, going on to race for McLaren, Mercedes, and Ferrari across a career spanning 2007-present. Holds the all-time F1 records for most wins, poles and podiums; moved to Ferrari in 2025. Across 393 Grand Prix starts, Hamilton took 106 race wins and scored 5201.5 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 206 podium finishes, 104 pole positions, and 69 fastest laps, and he won 7 World Championships. His time in Formula 1 is remembered as part of a career that left a lasting mark on the sport. He is often compared to Stirling Moss, whose career total sits at 186.64 championship points.

Michael Schumacher is a German driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1991, going on to race for Jordan, Benetton, Ferrari, and Mercedes across a career spanning 1991-2006, 2010-2012. First driver in history to win seven World Championships, five of them consecutively with Ferrari (2000-2004). Across 308 Grand Prix starts, Schumacher took 91 race wins and scored 1566.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 155 podium finishes, 68 pole positions, and 77 fastest laps, and he won 7 World Championships. He is often compared to Sebastian Vettel, whose career total sits at 3098.0 championship points.

Max Verstappen is a Dutch driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 2015, going on to race for Toro Rosso and Red Bull across a career spanning 2015-present. Became the youngest driver ever to start an F1 race (2015) and the youngest ever race winner (2016 Spanish GP). Across 233 Grand Prix starts, Verstappen took 71 race wins and scored 3556.5 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 131 podium finishes, 48 pole positions, and 37 fastest laps, and he won 4 World Championships. He is often compared to Keke Rosberg, whose career total sits at 159.5 championship points.

Sebastian Vettel is a German driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 2007, going on to race for BMW Sauber, Toro Rosso, Red Bull, Ferrari, and Aston Martin across a career spanning 2007-2022. Became the youngest World Champion in history in 2010 at age 23, a record later broken by Verstappen. Across 300 Grand Prix starts, Vettel took 53 race wins and scored 3098.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 122 podium finishes, 57 pole positions, and 38 fastest laps, and he won 4 World Championships. He is often compared to Nico Rosberg, whose career total sits at 1594.5 championship points.

Alain Prost is a French driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1980, going on to race for McLaren, Renault, and Williams across a career spanning 1980-1993. Nicknamed 'The Professor' for his calculating, fuel-efficient driving style; central figure in F1's fiercest rivalry with Ayrton Senna. Across 199 Grand Prix starts, Prost took 51 race wins and scored 798.5 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 106 podium finishes, 33 pole positions, and 41 fastest laps, and he won 4 World Championships. He is often compared to Ayrton Senna, whose career total sits at 614.0 championship points.

Ayrton Senna is a Brazilian driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1984, going on to race for Toleman, Lotus, McLaren, and Williams across a career spanning 1984-1994. Died from injuries sustained in a crash at the 1994 San Marino Grand Prix; widely regarded as one of the greatest drivers ever. Across 161 Grand Prix starts, Senna took 41 race wins and scored 614.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 80 podium finishes, 65 pole positions, and 19 fastest laps, and he won 3 World Championships. He is often compared to James Hunt, whose career total sits at 179.0 championship points.

Fernando Alonso is a Spanish driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 2001, going on to race for Minardi, Renault, McLaren, Ferrari, Alpine, and Aston Martin across a career spanning 2001-2018, 2021-present. Became the youngest double World Champion of his era (2005-2006); still competing in his 40s with Aston Martin. Across 441 Grand Prix starts, Alonso took 32 race wins and scored 2396.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 106 podium finishes, 22 pole positions, and 26 fastest laps, and he won 2 World Championships. He is often compared to George Russell, whose career total sits at 950.0 championship points.

Nigel Mansell is a British driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1980, going on to race for Lotus, Williams, and Ferrari across a career spanning 1980-1995. Won the 1992 title with a then-record nine wins in a season, then won the 1993 CART IndyCar title the following year. Across 187 Grand Prix starts, Mansell took 31 race wins and scored 482.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 59 podium finishes, 32 pole positions, and 30 fastest laps, and he won 1 World Championship. He is often compared to Alain Prost, whose career total sits at 798.5 championship points.

Jackie Stewart is a British driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1965, going on to race for BRM, Matra, and Tyrrell across a career spanning 1965-1973. Pioneered major driver-safety reforms in motorsport after witnessing numerous fatal crashes during his career. Across 99 Grand Prix starts, Stewart took 27 race wins and scored 360.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 43 podium finishes, 17 pole positions, and 15 fastest laps, and he won 3 World Championships. His time in Formula 1 is remembered as part of a career that left a lasting mark on the sport. He is often compared to Charles Leclerc, whose career total sits at 1827.0 championship points.

Jim Clark is a British driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1960, going on to race for Lotus across a career spanning 1960-1968. Died in a Formula 2 crash at Hockenheim in 1968; regarded as one of the most naturally gifted drivers of all time. Across 72 Grand Prix starts, Clark took 25 race wins and scored 274.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 32 podium finishes, 33 pole positions, and 28 fastest laps, and he won 2 World Championships. He is often compared to Kimi Raikkonen, whose career total sits at 1873.0 championship points.

Juan Manuel Fangio is an Argentine driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1950, going on to race for Alfa Romeo, Maserati, Mercedes, and Ferrari across a career spanning 1950-1958. Held the record for most World Championships (5) for nearly 50 years; his career win percentage (~46%) remains the highest ever. Across 51 Grand Prix starts, Fangio took 24 race wins and scored 277.64 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 35 podium finishes, 29 pole positions, and 23 fastest laps, and he won 5 World Championships. He is often compared to Nico Rosberg, whose career total sits at 1594.5 championship points.

Niki Lauda is an Austrian driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1971, going on to race for March, BRM, Ferrari, Brabham, and McLaren across a career spanning 1971-1979, 1982-1985. Survived a horrific fiery crash at the 1976 German GP and returned to racing just six weeks later. Across 171 Grand Prix starts, Lauda took 25 race wins and scored 420.5 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 54 podium finishes, 24 pole positions, and 24 fastest laps, and he won 3 World Championships. He is often compared to Daniel Ricciardo, whose career total sits at 1329.0 championship points.

Nelson Piquet is a Brazilian driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1978, going on to race for Ensign, McLaren, Brabham, Williams, Lotus, and Benetton across a career spanning 1978-1991. Three-time World Champion known for a laid-back public persona and a bitter rivalry with teammate Nigel Mansell at Williams. Across 204 Grand Prix starts, Piquet took 23 race wins and scored 485.5 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 60 podium finishes, 24 pole positions, and 23 fastest laps, and he won 3 World Championships. He is often compared to Jackie Stewart, whose career total sits at 360.0 championship points.

Damon Hill is a British driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1992, going on to race for Brabham, Williams, Arrows, and Jordan across a career spanning 1992-1999. Son of two-time champion Graham Hill; remains the only son of a World Champion to win his own title. Across 122 Grand Prix starts, Hill took 22 race wins and scored 360.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 42 podium finishes, 20 pole positions, and 19 fastest laps, and he won 1 World Championship. He is often compared to Ayrton Senna, whose career total sits at 614.0 championship points.

Mika Hakkinen is a Finnish driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1991, going on to race for Lotus and McLaren across a career spanning 1991-2001. Nicknamed 'The Flying Finn'; won back-to-back titles in 1998 and 1999 in a fierce rivalry with Michael Schumacher. Across 165 Grand Prix starts, Hakkinen took 20 race wins and scored 420.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 51 podium finishes, 26 pole positions, and 25 fastest laps, and he won 2 World Championships. His time in Formula 1 is remembered as part of a career that left a lasting mark on the sport. He is often compared to George Russell, whose career total sits at 950.0 championship points.

Jacques Villeneuve is a Canadian driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1996, going on to race for Williams, BAR, Renault, and Sauber across a career spanning 1996-2006. Son of legendary Ferrari driver Gilles Villeneuve; also won the 1995 Indianapolis 500 before his F1 title in 1997. Across 165 Grand Prix starts, Villeneuve took 11 race wins and scored 235.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 23 podium finishes, 13 pole positions, and 9 fastest laps, and he won 1 World Championship. He is often compared to Max Verstappen, whose career total sits at 3556.5 championship points.

Kimi Raikkonen is a Finnish driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 2001, going on to race for Sauber, McLaren, Ferrari, Lotus, and Alfa Romeo across a career spanning 2001-2009, 2012-2021. Nicknamed 'The Iceman' for his famously laconic radio messages; won the 2007 title in his first season with Ferrari. Across 353 Grand Prix starts, Raikkonen took 21 race wins and scored 1873.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 103 podium finishes, 18 pole positions, and 46 fastest laps, and he won 1 World Championship. He is often compared to Sergio Perez, whose career total sits at 1638.0 championship points.

Jenson Button is a British driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 2000, going on to race for Williams, Benetton/Renault, BAR, Honda, Brawn, and McLaren across a career spanning 2000-2016. Won the 2009 World Championship driving for Brawn GP, a team that existed for only that single season. Across 309 Grand Prix starts, Button took 15 race wins and scored 1235.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 50 podium finishes, 8 pole positions, and 8 fastest laps, and he won 1 World Championship. He is often compared to Mika Hakkinen, whose career total sits at 420.0 championship points.

Nico Rosberg is a German driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 2006, going on to race for Williams and Mercedes across a career spanning 2006-2016. Retired just five days after clinching his only World Championship title in 2016, at the height of his career. Across 206 Grand Prix starts, Rosberg took 23 race wins and scored 1594.5 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 57 podium finishes, 30 pole positions, and 20 fastest laps, and he won 1 World Championship. He is often compared to Graham Hill, whose career total sits at 289.0 championship points.

Emerson Fittipaldi is a Brazilian driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1970, going on to race for Lotus, McLaren, and Fittipaldi across a career spanning 1970-1980. Became the youngest World Champion of his era in 1972 (age 25); later won the Indianapolis 500 twice. Across 144 Grand Prix starts, Fittipaldi took 14 race wins and scored 281.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 35 podium finishes, 6 pole positions, and 6 fastest laps, and he won 2 World Championships. He is often compared to Jochen Rindt, whose career total sits at 109.0 championship points.

Graham Hill is a British driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1958, going on to race for Lotus, BRM, Brabham, and Embassy Hill across a career spanning 1958-1975. The only driver to win motorsport's 'Triple Crown': the Monaco Grand Prix, the Indianapolis 500 and the 24 Hours of Le Mans. Across 176 Grand Prix starts, Hill took 14 race wins and scored 289.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 36 podium finishes, 13 pole positions, and 13 fastest laps, and he won 2 World Championships. He is often compared to Carlos Sainz Jr., whose career total sits at 1100.0 championship points.

Jack Brabham is an Australian driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1955, going on to race for Cooper and Brabham across a career spanning 1955-1970. The only driver in history to win a World Championship in a car built by his own team (Brabham, 1966). Across 126 Grand Prix starts, Brabham took 14 race wins and scored 261.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 31 podium finishes, 13 pole positions, and 12 fastest laps, and he won 3 World Championships. He is often compared to Alberto Ascari, whose career total sits at 140.64 championship points.

Denny Hulme is a New Zealander who made his Formula 1 debut in 1965, going on to race for Brabham and McLaren across a career spanning 1965-1974. Nicknamed 'The Bear'; died of a heart attack while competing in a touring car race at Bathurst in 1992. Across 112 Grand Prix starts, Hulme took 8 race wins and scored 248.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 33 podium finishes, 1 pole position, and 9 fastest laps, and he won 1 World Championship. He is often compared to John Surtees, whose career total sits at 189.0 championship points.

James Hunt is a British driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1973, going on to race for Hesketh, McLaren, and Wolf across a career spanning 1973-1979. Won the dramatic 1976 title battle against Niki Lauda by a single point, later dramatized in the film 'Rush.'. Across 92 Grand Prix starts, Hunt took 10 race wins and scored 179.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 23 podium finishes, 14 pole positions, and 8 fastest laps, and he won 1 World Championship. He is often compared to Keke Rosberg, whose career total sits at 159.5 championship points.

Mario Andretti is an American driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1968, going on to race for Lotus, March, Ferrari, Parnelli, Williams, and Alfa Romeo across a career spanning 1968-1972, 1974-1982. The only driver to win an F1 World Championship, the Indianapolis 500 and the Daytona 500 across his career. Across 128 Grand Prix starts, Andretti took 12 race wins and scored 180.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 19 podium finishes, 18 pole positions, and 10 fastest laps, and he won 1 World Championship. He is often compared to Alain Prost, whose career total sits at 798.5 championship points.

Jody Scheckter is a South African driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1972, going on to race for McLaren, Tyrrell, Wolf, and Ferrari across a career spanning 1972-1980. Was Ferrari's last World Champion before Michael Schumacher, a gap of 21 years, winning the 1979 title. Across 112 Grand Prix starts, Scheckter took 10 race wins and scored 255.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 33 podium finishes, 3 pole positions, and 5 fastest laps, and he won 1 World Championship. He is often compared to Alain Prost, whose career total sits at 798.5 championship points.

Alan Jones is an Australian driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1975, going on to race for Hesketh, Hill, Surtees, Shadow, and Williams across a career spanning 1975-1986. Won the 1980 World Championship with Williams; son of 1950s Australian racer Stan Jones. Across 116 Grand Prix starts, Jones took 12 race wins and scored 206.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 24 podium finishes, 6 pole positions, and 13 fastest laps, and he won 1 World Championship. His time in Formula 1 is remembered as part of a career that left a lasting mark on the sport. He is often compared to Juan Pablo Montoya, whose career total sits at 307.0 championship points.

Keke Rosberg is a Finnish driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1978, going on to race for Theodore, Wolf, Fittipaldi, ATS, Williams, and McLaren across a career spanning 1978-1986. Won the 1982 title with only a single race win, the lowest win total of any champion; father of Nico Rosberg. Across 114 Grand Prix starts, Rosberg took 5 race wins and scored 159.5 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 17 podium finishes, 5 pole positions, and 3 fastest laps, and he won 1 World Championship. He is often compared to Felipe Massa, whose career total sits at 1167.0 championship points.

Giuseppe Farina is an Italian driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1950, going on to race for Alfa Romeo and Ferrari across a career spanning 1950-1955. Won the very first Formula 1 World Championship in 1950 driving for Alfa Romeo. Across 33 Grand Prix starts, Farina took 5 race wins and scored 89.67 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 20 podium finishes, 5 pole positions, and 5 fastest laps, and he won 1 World Championship. His time in Formula 1 is remembered as part of a career that left a lasting mark on the sport. He is often compared to Nigel Mansell, whose career total sits at 482.0 championship points.

Alberto Ascari is an Italian driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1950, going on to race for Ferrari and Lancia across a career spanning 1950-1955. Won nine consecutive Grands Prix, a record that stood for decades; died testing a Ferrari sports car in 1955. Across 32 Grand Prix starts, Ascari took 13 race wins and scored 140.64 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 17 podium finishes, 14 pole positions, and 12 fastest laps, and he won 2 World Championships. He is often compared to Graham Hill, whose career total sits at 289.0 championship points.

Mike Hawthorn is a British driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1952, going on to race for Cooper, Connaught, Ferrari, and Vanwall across a career spanning 1952-1958. Britain's first F1 World Champion (1958); retired from racing immediately after and died in a road accident months later. Across 45 Grand Prix starts, Hawthorn took 3 race wins and scored 127.64 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 18 podium finishes, 4 pole positions, and 6 fastest laps, and he won 1 World Championship. He is often compared to Alain Prost, whose career total sits at 798.5 championship points.

John Surtees is a British driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1960, going on to race for Lotus, Cooper, Ferrari, Honda, and BRM across a career spanning 1960-1972. The only person to win World Championships on both two wheels (motorcycle Grand Prix racing) and four wheels (F1). Across 111 Grand Prix starts, Surtees took 6 race wins and scored 189.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 24 podium finishes, 8 pole positions, and 11 fastest laps, and he won 1 World Championship. He is often compared to Jenson Button, whose career total sits at 1235.0 championship points.

Jochen Rindt is an Austrian driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1964, going on to race for Rob Walker, Cooper, Brabham, and Lotus across a career spanning 1964-1970. Formula 1's only posthumous World Champion, having died in practice at Monza before the 1970 season concluded. Across 60 Grand Prix starts, Rindt took 6 race wins and scored 109.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 13 podium finishes, 10 pole positions, and 3 fastest laps, and he won 1 World Championship. He is often compared to Daniel Ricciardo, whose career total sits at 1329.0 championship points.

Charles Leclerc is a Monegasque driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 2018, going on to race for Sauber and Ferrari across a career spanning 2018-present. Became Ferrari's youngest ever pole-sitter and finally won his home Monaco Grand Prix in 2024 after years of near-misses. Across 173 Grand Prix starts, Leclerc took 8 race wins and scored 1827.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 54 podium finishes, 26 pole positions, and 8 fastest laps, and he has not yet won a World Championship. He is often compared to Giuseppe Farina, whose career total sits at 89.67 championship points.

Lando Norris is a British driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 2019, going on to race for McLaren across a career spanning 2019-present. Won his first Formula 1 World Championship in 2025 driving for McLaren after several years as a championship contender. Across 151 Grand Prix starts, Norris took 8 race wins and scored 1589.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 40 podium finishes, 18 pole positions, and 11 fastest laps, and he won 1 World Championship. His time in Formula 1 is remembered as part of a career that left a lasting mark on the sport. He is often compared to James Hunt, whose career total sits at 179.0 championship points.

Oscar Piastri is an Australian driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 2023, going on to race for McLaren across a career spanning 2023-present. Won junior titles in Formula Renault Eurocup, F3 (2020) and F2 (2021) in his rookie seasons of each before nearly winning the 2025 F1 title. Across 70 Grand Prix starts, Piastri took 9 race wins and scored 700.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 26 podium finishes, 9 pole positions, and 5 fastest laps, and he has not yet won a World Championship. He is often compared to Kimi Raikkonen, whose career total sits at 1873.0 championship points.

George Russell is a British driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 2019, going on to race for Williams and Mercedes across a career spanning 2019-present. Won his first Grand Prix at the 2022 Brazilian GP for Mercedes after replacing Lewis Hamilton's former seat. Across 152 Grand Prix starts, Russell took 4 race wins and scored 950.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 22 podium finishes, 4 pole positions, and 5 fastest laps, and he has not yet won a World Championship. He is often compared to Nelson Piquet, whose career total sits at 485.5 championship points.

Carlos Sainz Jr. is a Spanish driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 2015, going on to race for Toro Rosso, Renault, McLaren, Ferrari, and Williams across a career spanning 2015-present. Son of two-time World Rally Champion Carlos Sainz Sr.; took his first F1 win at the 2022 British Grand Prix for Ferrari. Across 215 Grand Prix starts, Jr. took 4 race wins and scored 1100.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 27 podium finishes, 6 pole positions, and 4 fastest laps, and he has not yet won a World Championship. He is often compared to Jim Clark, whose career total sits at 274.0 championship points.

Sergio Perez is a Mexican driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 2011, going on to race for Sauber, McLaren, Force India, Racing Point, and Red Bull across a career spanning 2011-2024. Mexico's most successful F1 driver, nicknamed 'Checo,' known for exceptional tyre-management ability. Across 298 Grand Prix starts, Perez took 6 race wins and scored 1638.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 39 podium finishes, 3 pole positions, and 11 fastest laps, and he has not yet won a World Championship. He is often compared to Jenson Button, whose career total sits at 1235.0 championship points.

Valtteri Bottas is a Finnish driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 2013, going on to race for Williams, Mercedes, and Alfa Romeo/Sauber across a career spanning 2013-present. Partnered Lewis Hamilton at Mercedes for five seasons, finishing championship runner-up in 2019 and 2020. Across 242 Grand Prix starts, Bottas took 10 race wins and scored 1797.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 67 podium finishes, 20 pole positions, and 20 fastest laps, and he has not yet won a World Championship. He is often compared to Jochen Rindt, whose career total sits at 109.0 championship points.

Daniel Ricciardo is an Australian driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 2011, going on to race for HRT, Toro Rosso, Red Bull, Renault, McLaren, and RB across a career spanning 2011-2024. Known for his trademark 'Shoey' victory celebration, drinking champagne from his racing boot after wins. Across 257 Grand Prix starts, Ricciardo took 8 race wins and scored 1329.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 32 podium finishes, 3 pole positions, and 20 fastest laps, and he has not yet won a World Championship. He is often compared to Jim Clark, whose career total sits at 274.0 championship points.

Stirling Moss is a British driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1951, going on to race for HWM, Maserati, Mercedes, Vanwall, Cooper, and Lotus across a career spanning 1951-1961. Widely regarded as the greatest F1 driver never to win a World Championship, finishing runner-up in the standings four times. Across 66 Grand Prix starts, Moss took 16 race wins and scored 186.64 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 24 podium finishes, 16 pole positions, and 19 fastest laps, and he has not yet won a World Championship. He is often compared to John Surtees, whose career total sits at 189.0 championship points.

David Coulthard is a British driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1994, going on to race for Williams, McLaren, and Red Bull across a career spanning 1994-2008. One of the most consistent points-scorers of his era; later became a prominent Formula 1 broadcaster and pundit. Across 246 Grand Prix starts, Coulthard took 13 race wins and scored 535.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 62 podium finishes, 12 pole positions, and 18 fastest laps, and he has not yet won a World Championship. He is often compared to Riccardo Patrese, whose career total sits at 281.0 championship points.

Rubens Barrichello is a Brazilian driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1993, going on to race for Jordan, Stewart, Ferrari, Honda, Brawn, and Williams across a career spanning 1993-2011. Held the record for most Grand Prix starts (322) at his retirement; spent six seasons as Michael Schumacher's Ferrari teammate. Across 326 Grand Prix starts, Barrichello took 11 race wins and scored 658.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 68 podium finishes, 14 pole positions, and 17 fastest laps, and he has not yet won a World Championship. He is often compared to Nelson Piquet, whose career total sits at 485.5 championship points.

Felipe Massa is a Brazilian driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 2002, going on to race for Sauber, Ferrari, and Williams across a career spanning 2002, 2004-2017. Lost the 2008 World Championship to Lewis Hamilton by a single point on the final corner of the final race of the season. Across 272 Grand Prix starts, Massa took 11 race wins and scored 1167.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 41 podium finishes, 16 pole positions, and 15 fastest laps, and he has not yet won a World Championship. He is often compared to Michael Schumacher, whose career total sits at 1566.0 championship points.

Gerhard Berger is an Austrian driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1984, going on to race for ATS, Arrows, Benetton, Ferrari, and McLaren across a career spanning 1984-1997. Close friend and practical-joke partner of Ayrton Senna during their years together as McLaren teammates. Across 210 Grand Prix starts, Berger took 10 race wins and scored 385.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 48 podium finishes, 12 pole positions, and 21 fastest laps, and he has not yet won a World Championship. He is often compared to Jim Clark, whose career total sits at 274.0 championship points.

Mark Webber is an Australian driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 2002, going on to race for Minardi, Jaguar, Williams, and Red Bull across a career spanning 2002-2013. Finished runner-up in the 2010 World Championship to his own teammate Sebastian Vettel; later a successful sports car racer. Across 215 Grand Prix starts, Webber took 9 race wins and scored 1047.5 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 42 podium finishes, 13 pole positions, and 19 fastest laps, and he has not yet won a World Championship. He is often compared to Jody Scheckter, whose career total sits at 255.0 championship points.

Riccardo Patrese is an Italian driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1977, going on to race for Shadow, Arrows, Brabham, Alfa Romeo, Williams, and Benetton across a career spanning 1977-1993. Held the record for most Grand Prix starts (256) at his retirement, a record that stood for more than a decade. Across 256 Grand Prix starts, Patrese took 6 race wins and scored 281.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 37 podium finishes, 8 pole positions, and 8 fastest laps, and he has not yet won a World Championship. He is often compared to Ayrton Senna, whose career total sits at 614.0 championship points.

Ronnie Peterson is a Swedish driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 1970, going on to race for March, Lotus, and Tyrrell across a career spanning 1970-1978. Known as 'SuperSwede' for his spectacular car-control and sideways driving style; died from injuries in a crash at the 1978 Italian GP. Across 123 Grand Prix starts, Peterson took 10 race wins and scored 206.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 26 podium finishes, 14 pole positions, and 9 fastest laps, and he has not yet won a World Championship. He is often compared to Damon Hill, whose career total sits at 360.0 championship points.

Juan Pablo Montoya is a Colombian driver who made his Formula 1 debut in 2001, going on to race for Williams and McLaren across a career spanning 2001-2006. Won the 1999 CART championship and the 2000 Indianapolis 500 before moving to F1; later successful in NASCAR. Across 94 Grand Prix starts, Montoya took 7 race wins and scored 307.0 career championship points. Over that span he also picked up 30 podium finishes, 13 pole positions, and 12 fastest laps, and he has not yet won a World Championship. He is often compared to Ayrton Senna, whose career total sits at 614.0 championship points.
